newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SKF says to be part of industry changes.
newsitem.headline: SKF says to be part of industry changes.

text.p: The world's bearings industry will continue to be restructured and Sweden's SKF will be part of that process, the company's managing director Peter Augustsson said on Tuesday.
But he denied any plans for SKF to be involved in any large deals.
"Restructuring of the sector will continue and SKF will be part of that. One example is our purchase of 20 percent in China's Wafangdian Bearing Company," Augustsson told Reuters.
But he did not think SKF had anything to benefit from buying any of its large rivals.
However he did not want to exclude any of the other European companies from being part of a restructuring deal.
"Renault has announced that it wants to do something with its bearings company SNR. Also there are rumours in some parts that someone will buy German FAG Kugelfischer ", sade Augustsson.
He said SKF was not interested in buying the German company.
"I cannot see why we would want to increase our focus on Europe and towards the car industry," he said.
Augustsson said it was possible some Japanese players could be interested in this company.
"If there is to be a big deal then it is most likely that some Japanese company will go in and buy. Of these the one with the most financial muscle is NSK."

SKF's share price has risen in recent weeks amid market speculation that it could be the next company in the powerful Wallenberg stable to undergo a shakeup after appliance maker Electrolux announced a radical restructuring package in early June that was well received by the market.

SKF shares were trading 4.5 crowns higher at 216.5 crowns at 0930 GMT Tuesday after the company posted a lower profit after financial items for the first half of 1997 but said improving trends were continuing.
